record.original_question: Develop software to generate benchmark parameterized linear systems that are generally accepted as relevant in practice and suitable for theoretical analysis.

evidence.quote: Develop software to generate benchmark parameterized linear systems that are generally accepted as relevant in practice and suitable for theoretical analysis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A parameterized linear system is a family of linear systems of the form A(p) x = b(p), where p = (p_1, ..., p_k) ranges over a parameter domain P ⊂ R^k (or C^k), A(p) is an n × n matrix whose entries depend on p, and b(p) is an n-vector whose entries depend on p; the entries are typically given as polynomial, rational, or interval-valued functions of the parameters. Design and implement a software framework that automatically generates benchmark instances of such parameterized linear systems satisfying the following requirements:

(1) The generated families are representative of problems arising in engineering and scientific practice (e.g., from structural analysis, electrical networks, control theory, discretized PDEs with uncertain coefficients, or interval/affine parametric models), so that they are widely accepted as practically relevant test cases.

(2) The generated families are simultaneously suitable for rigorous theoretical analysis, meaning that each instance is accompanied by a precise mathematical specification (parameter domain, dependency functions, structural properties such as symmetry, sparsity pattern, conditioning bounds, solution-set descriptions where applicable) sufficient to permit proofs of correctness and complexity bounds for solvers acting on it.

(3) The generator is parameterized itself (allowing control over dimension n, number of parameters k, type of dependency, conditioning, and structural features) and produces reproducible instances together with reference solutions or solution enclosures.

Provide such a generator and justify that the produced benchmark suite meets criteria (1)–(3).
artifact.status_search_result: The task is a software/benchmarking development goal rather than a closed-form mathematical conjecture. No widely accepted, comprehensive benchmark generator for parameterized linear systems meeting both practical relevance and theoretical-analysis suitability appears to have been established; while individual test collections (e.g., interval/parametric examples in INTLAB, examples in the literature on parametric linear systems) exist, a general-purpose generator as described remains an open research/engineering goal.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized linear systems and interval methods
status_evidence.snippet: INTLAB provides routines for parametric interval linear systems but not a general benchmark generator.
status_evidence.claim: Existing tools handle specific parametric linear system instances but do not constitute a comprehensive benchmark generator.
